title: 在训狗中学到的控制权与人性(1)
desc: 在训狗中学到的控制权与人性(1)

paragraphs.en: When I carried my beautiful two-month-old puppy into our home for the first time, I couldn't have imagined the scene six months later, as I led her through my local park experiencing such a toxic cocktail of emotions – guilt, regret, powerlessness – that I had tears in my eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 当我第一次把两个月大、漂亮的小狗抱进家门时，根本想象不到六个月后的场景：我牵着她穿行在本地公园，心中交织着种种糟透了的情绪——愧疚、懊悔、无力感，泪水在眼眶打转。

paragraphs.en: It was a walk that many dog owners will recognise as having "gone badly".
paragraphs.zh: 很多养狗的人都懂，这就是一场“彻底搞砸”的遛狗经历。

paragraphs.en: My exuberant dog, Dusty, had approached another dog that did not wish to play with her.
paragraphs.zh: 我精力旺盛的狗狗达斯蒂，凑向了另一只不想和她玩耍的狗。

paragraphs.en: This shouldn't have happened. I should have been able to call her back.
paragraphs.zh: 这本不该发生。我本该把她唤回来。

paragraphs.en: Maybe I should have just kept her on the lead. Maybe I shouldn't have got a dog in the first place.
paragraphs.zh: 或许我就该一直牵着牵引绳。或许我从一开始就不该养狗。

paragraphs.en: Dusty started barking, jumping and circling the owner and her dog at high speed.
paragraphs.zh: 达斯蒂开始吠叫、蹦跳，高速围着那只狗和它的主人转圈。

paragraphs.en: "Do you want to have a dogfight?" the owner asked curtly, while I lunged around on the ground, all dignity jettisoned.
paragraphs.zh: “你想让它们打起来吗？”那位女主人语气生硬地质问，而我在地上扑来扑去，体面荡然无存。

paragraphs.en: "My dog just wants to play with yours," I protested. "But mine doesn't want to play," she replied.
paragraphs.zh: “我的狗只是想和你的狗玩，”我辩解道。对方答道：“可我的狗不想。”

paragraphs.en: "If you just let yours off the lead for a moment," I countered, "I think mine would calm down. I promise you, she's not aggressive."
paragraphs.zh: “你放开你的狗一会儿试试，”我反驳，“我觉得我的狗会冷静下来。我向你保证，她没有攻击性。”

paragraphs.en: Her reply: "So what do you call this?" Checkmate.
paragraphs.zh: 她反问：“那你管这叫什么？”一句话，我哑口无言。

paragraphs.en: As the seconds and then minutes passed, with Dusty still evading my reach, I began to wonder how long this might go on.
paragraphs.zh: 一秒秒过去，接着是几分钟，达斯蒂始终能躲开我的抓捕，我开始担心这场闹剧会持续多久。

paragraphs.en: Would the police have to be called?
paragraphs.zh: 要不要报警？

paragraphs.en: I can't remember the precise lunge that successfully brought Dusty back under my control but eventually I managed it, attaching her lead and heading for home, determined never to put myself or anyone else in that situation again.
paragraphs.zh: 我记不清是哪一次猛扑终于控制住了达斯蒂，但我最终抓到了她，扣上牵引绳往家走，下定决心再也不让自己和其他人陷入这样的处境。

paragraphs.en: As any parent of a toddler knows, being morally liable for something that is incapable of moral liability is a fraught and stressful business.
paragraphs.zh: 所有带幼儿的家长都明白，为一个没有道德判断能力的生命承担道义责任，是一件充满煎熬与压力的事。

paragraphs.en: It forces one to develop a range of imperfect techniques that are all fundamentally about one thing: control.
paragraphs.zh: 这迫使你摸索出一系列并不完美的办法，而这些办法本质上都指向一件事：控制。

paragraphs.en: Controlling a dog, like controlling a small child, requires a mixture of training, routine, incentives, rewards and physical constraints.
paragraphs.zh: 管教狗狗，就像照看小孩子，需要训练、规律作息、激励、奖励，再加上物理约束多管齐下。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes you just need to pick the darn thing up.
paragraphs.zh: 有时候你只能干脆把这小家伙抱起来。

paragraphs.en: There is no shortage of advice on how to do it, but little of it recognises the hardest aspect: the feelings of desperation, frustration, shame and resentment that an adult feels when it all goes wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 相关的建议多如牛毛，但很少有人提及最艰难的部分：当一切失控时，成年人心中涌起的绝望、挫败、羞耻与愤懑。

paragraphs.en: We are all familiar with the cliches of Britain as a "nation of animal lovers", but we often overlook quite how weird and remarkable it is that we have, for the most part successfully, integrated a vast number of autonomous, non-human entities into a human system of rights and wrongs.
paragraphs.zh: 我们都听过这样的陈词滥调，说英国是一个“热爱动物的国度”，但我们常常忽略一件奇妙又了不起的事：大体上，我们成功把大量拥有自主意识的非人类生命，纳入人类的是非体系之中。

paragraphs.en: As I tried to integrate Dusty into that system, however, I discovered how difficult and fraught the process is.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，就在我试着把达斯蒂融入这套体系时，才发现这个过程何其艰难、充满波折。

paragraphs.en: I also began to see how much of what I write and think about in my professional life as a sociologist – power, behaviour and control – reflected what goes on in the world of dog training.
paragraphs.zh: 身为社会学家，我研究和思考的许多专业议题——权力、行为、控制，也让我渐渐发现，这些都和训犬世界发生的一切遥相呼应。

paragraphs.en: Control is a watchword of our times.
paragraphs.zh: 控制，是我们这个时代的关键词。

paragraphs.en: The Brexit referendum, which took place 10 years ago this week, was famously won on a promise to take it back.
paragraphs.zh: 十年前的这周举行的脱欧公投，最出名的口号就是夺回控制权。

paragraphs.en: Apps and smart devices are sold as ways of extending control over the minutiae of our time, households, finances and bodies.
paragraphs.zh: 各类应用程序与智能设备在售卖时，都宣称可以帮我们掌控时间、家庭、财务与身体的细枝末节。

paragraphs.en: People are increasingly controlled at the workplace by intrusive systems of surveillance and behavioural intervention, while the AI revolution poses an even greater challenge, of how to bring powerful post-human agents under human control.
paragraphs.zh: 职场上，人们越来越受到侵入式监控与行为干预系统的管控；而人工智能革命带来更大的难题：如何让强大的后人类智能体，处于人类的掌控之下。

paragraphs.en: But the amount of time and money we spend striving for control is indicative of how close we feel to losing it.
paragraphs.zh: 但我们耗费大量时间金钱去追逐掌控感，恰恰说明我们总觉得自己快要失去它。

paragraphs.en: And nowhere is this more true than with dogs.
paragraphs.zh: 在养狗这件事上，这一点体现得淋漓尽致。
